--- import Information from "../layouts/Information.astro"; ---

This page describes a proposed sponsorship idea for elixir.menu. It is business information, not part of the independent tool recommendations. No sponsor is active, and the sponsor formats described here are not approved or available yet.

How a coding agent uses elixir.menu

A coding agent fetches the agent instructions and the resource index, reads only the guides that match the application’s requirements, and chooses tools for the task. Existing project decisions and installed-version documentation come first. Recommendations, alternatives and their independent criteria stay as they are.

Where an optional sponsor could fit

A sponsor is optional and disclosed. If a sponsor is relevant to the task, an agent could mention it next to the independent recommendation, clearly labelled as a sponsor. The user keeps the choice, and the agent still presents alternatives. Agent behavior like this is not available today.

Example workflow

Example: a coding agent is asked to add background jobs to a Phoenix application. It reads the optional tools guide, recommends Oban for durable work, and explains the integration. If a relevant sponsor existed, the agent would label it as a sponsor, say why it is relevant, and leave the decision to the user. This is an illustration only.

Visitor protections

  • A sponsor is always disclosed with a clear label.
  • A sponsor never changes rankings, alternatives or the independent criteria.
  • The user keeps the choice, and sponsors are not added to the tool exports.

Ask about sponsoring

For pricing and audience numbers, email consulting@optimum.ba. Commercial details stay in that conversation.
